reason: Re-opened packet.js pali 25: Story XXV.10 (The Monk and the Ragged Garment, Norman [115] to [116]) has every quoted phrase of the evidence verbatim (loin-cloth and plow hung on the tree, admonishing himself at its foot whenever discontented, Arahatship within days, the Teacher: My son has admonished himself by himself). The Pali Tattha (attanāva attānaṃ codaya sāraya) agrees. The paraphrase (former ploughman, rags on the tree, self-admonition whenever discontent came, and so arahatship) is carried by the story and the Teacher’s own words; spoken for is fair, since the Teacher speaks 379 to 380 in answer to the monks’ charge against him. Plain sense (late in the chapter, addresses the bhikkhu directly) is true to day.js 379 and uses none of its words. verse.js ok (ref Dhammapada 379, at 378); entry-check ok. Minor only: whenever discontent came sits after where his old rags hung and can be misparsed; not a refutation.
